LESSON: DRAWING FROM MAKING

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PICTURE
Topic 1.2: Drawing from MAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Drawing from MAKING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you use MAKING memory the learner should be able to; materials for drawing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DRAWING FROM MAKING
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Drawing from MAKING helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DRAWING FROM MAKING
Study Drawing from MAKING like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like

What this means
In this part you learn to identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Drawing from MAKING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Drawing from MAKING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Drawing from MAKING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Drawing from MAKING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Drawing from MAKING from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Drawing from MAKING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Drawing from MAKING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you use MAKING memory the learner should be able to; materials for drawing?
2. how to use 2. Why do you like b) use appropriate tools to drawing tools. drawing?
3. What would you c) draw symbolic memory like to draw?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Drawing from MAKING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify drawing materials • Learners to be guided on how to use 2. Why do you like.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
